text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Cabinet rejects transport and finance ministers' plan to privatise the national airport Schiphol. (p1)
- Entertainment group Endemol's net profit pressured by disappointing result of 'Holiday on Ice' show. (p1)
- Inflation in the Netherlands fell to two percent in March, against 2.2 pct in February. (p1)
- Catering companies BRN and Service One Catering are to merge so as better to react to the market's demands. (p1)
- Electronic chip tester Rood Technology sees the need for a partner. (p3)
- Publisher Audax 1996 net plummets to Dfl 240,000 from Dfl 6.9 million in 1995. (p1)
- Mould maker Axxicon sees 1997 Q1 results fall sharply from Dfl 1.6 million to Dfl 0.5 million. (p5)
- Dutch businesses are among the slowest in Europe to pay their bills, according to a study. (p7)
- VOLKSKRANT
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert wants to reduce tax for employers with workers who receive minimum wages. (p19)
- Traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma unexpectedly allows KPN's telecom arm PTT Telecom to bid for a new mobile phone licence. (p2)
- Shareholders' lobby group VEB wants a probe into why paper and packaging group KNP BT's revealed its disappointing Q1 results soo late. (p2)
- Chemicals, industrial services and transport concern Cindu International mulls splitting up its activites. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Social affairs minister wants to give chronically ill people a benefit of about 250 guilders from next year. (p1)
- Unions and chemicals concern Akzo Nobel agree on shorter working week. (p3)
- Chief of Grenswisselkantoren GWK, a subsidiary of bank insurer Fortis, suspected of embezzling millions of guilders. (p7)
- Bourse watchdog STE is to investigate options and share schemes for staff of bourse-listed companies. (p21) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Food wholesaler Sligro takes over rival Van der Velde. (p13)
- Philips Electroncis and Jordan to cooperate in making electrical toothbrushes. (p13) TROUW
- Cabinet considers putting aside Dfl 1.5 bn for new pension scheme. (p1)
- Rabobank offers help to pig farmers in financial trouble. (p7)
